//: 1. Node runs the sources and the tests directly. Node 22+ strips TypeScript types
from .ts files but does not resolve extensionless specifiers, so every relative
import in src/ and test/ carries an explicit '.ts'. allowImportingTsExtensions
accepts that, and rewriteRelativeImportExtensions (tsconfig.build.json) turns each
one back into '.js' in the emitted lib/, so the published package is ordinary
2. erasableSyntaxOnly forbids the TypeScript constructs Node cannot strip (enum,
namespace, parameter properties). That is not a limitation being worked around:
it is the rule that keeps the enum mirrors in src/enums.ts const objects, which
is what makes them comparable to pd.h by a test.
This file is the typecheck and editor configuration and covers the tests too;
tsconfig.build.json is the one that emits lib/. Metro consumes src/index.ts directly
(package.json 'react-native'), so an app never waits for that build.
